response.sql: SELECT ma.player_id AS manager_id, p.death_country, COUNT(*) AS award_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY p.death_country) AS share FROM manager_award ma JOIN player p ON p.player_id = ma.player_id WHERE p.death_country IS NOT NULL AND p.death_country <> '' GROUP BY ma.player_id, p.death_country ORDER BY share DESC NULLS LAST, manager_id LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Each row in manager_award is one award and counts once; the award count is COUNT(*) per manager and death country.
player.player_id is unique, so joining manager_award to player does not duplicate award rows.
'Empty string' means exactly '' with no trimming, so a whitespace-only death_country is kept as its own group.
The share denominator is the sum of award rows across all manager_award rows whose player has the same death_country, which is the same as the sum of the per-manager counts in that country.
